subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Rise and Fall of Quibi
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Rise and Fall of Quibi.

hook.text: Quibi raised $1.75 billion to build a streaming app for short-form video. It lasted six months.

buildup.text: Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman bet that people wanted ten-minute Hollywood episodes on their phones.

discovery.text: The app launched in April 2020—right as the pandemic began. People were stuck at home watching long-form TV.

twist.text: TikTok already owned the short-form market for free. Nobody wanted to pay for what they got elsewhere at no cost.

climax.text: Quibi shut down in December 2020. It became the fastest billion-dollar failure in entertainment history.

punchline.text: They spent two billion to learn that timing is everything.

quiz.question: Why did the streaming service Quibi fail so quickly?
options: It launched during a pandemic and competed with free short-form platforms
